statements.quote: Data will be made available on request.
statements.locator: p. 19, Data availability

statements.quote: We selected a fine-tuned LLM displaying startup ideas (Startup Ideas powered by OpenAI, 2022) generated with GPT-3 (Brown et al., 2020), the model preceding GPT-4.
statements.locator: p. 6, Section 4.2, LLM used for the experiment

statements.quote: Human feedback was incorporated through prompting a list of past ideas preceded each time by “Good idea:” or “Bad idea:” (see Appendix A for exact prompt).
statements.locator: p. 7, Section 4.2, reference to Appendix A

statements.quote: A total of 488 LLM-generated startup ideas were used to construct an idea database. Table 3 provides a list of 10 randomly extracted from the database. Ideas that were uncoherent or blatantly described an existing company were excluded, leaving 453 LLM-generated startup ideas to be used as stimuli.
statements.locator: p. 7, Section 4.2, stimulus database and Table 3

statements.quote: A scenario (see appendix B) was constructed to immerse participants in a realistic context while supporting external validity.
statements.locator: p. 7, Section 4.3, reference to Appendix B

statements.quote: To operationalize breadth of exploration, one of the authors read and categorized all generated ideas, ensuring qualitative rigor by inductively developing an auditable data structure showing advancement from data to findings (see Appendix C) (Gioia et al., 2013).
statements.locator: p. 7, Section 4.4.1, reference to Appendix C

statements.quote: Finally, Appendix D also reports alternative outcome measurements and post hoc analyses focused on the quantity and quality of the ideas.
statements.locator: p. 8, Section 4.4.2, reference to Appendix D

statements.quote: Because these outcome variables did not follow a normal distribution (see Appendix E), we used non-parametric tests, although parametric tests yield similar conclusions.
statements.locator: p. 8, Section 4.6.1, reference to Appendix E

statements.quote: Sentence embeddings were generated using the SpaCy package, and pairwise cosine similarity scores were computed.
statements.locator: p. 8, Section 4.6.2, software used for the semantic analysis

statements.quote: On top of these analyses, Appendix D reports additional analyses on alternative outcomes relating to idea quantity and quality.
statements.locator: p. 9, end of Section 4.6.2

statements.quote: We selected from the fine-tuned LLM 44 ideas related to education (relevant for the task described below) for our idea database. Again, the study was conducted before the public release of generative AI models, so participants could not use other generative AI tools. Table 5 provides a list of 10 randomly extracted ideas.
statements.locator: p. 9, Section 5.2, stimulus database and Table 5

statements.quote: In alignment with Study 1, one of the authors read and categorized all generated ideas (see Appendix C for the data structure).
statements.locator: p. 9, Section 5.4, reference to Appendix C

statements.quote: We again measured depth of exploration and report in Appendix D alternative outcome measurements and post hoc analyses focused on the quantity and quality of the ideas.
statements.locator: p. 9, Section 5.4, reference to Appendix D

statements.quote: Because the outcome variables did not follow a normal distribution (see Appendix E), we used a non-parametric Kruskal-Wallis test, although a parametric test yields the same conclusions.
statements.locator: p. 10, Section 5.5.1, reference to Appendix E

statements.quote: Analyses of novelty and usefulness ratings from experts, reported in Appendix D, show patterns consistent with the conclusion that task breadth is a boundary condition shaping the effects of LLM assistance on creative outcomes.
statements.locator: p. 11, Section 5.5.3, reference to Appendix D

notes:
Checked on 2026-10-09. Read the entire 139,579-character markdown conversion, including Appendices A-E and references, and checked the quoted passages directly against the 21-page PDF (Technovation 153 (2026), 103540). Quotes retain the PDF wording and punctuation, with line wrapping and line-end hyphenation normalized.

The paper explicitly says the data will be made available on request (p. 19). Neither the paper nor forms/c117.json data_and_code gives a data-repository or analysis-code URL. No preregistration or separate online supplementary-file link is stated. The acknowledgements on p. 13 mention feedback on earlier versions and AOM presentations but provide no data, code, or materials link.

Appendix A contains the generator prompt, Appendix B the experimental instructions, Appendix C semantic-category labels and aggregate counts, Appendix D aggregate participant-outcome summaries, and Appendix E normality tests and plots. Tables 3 and 5 give examples of AI-generated stimuli. These do not provide participant IDs, individual arm assignments, individual outcome records, or the participants' original idea texts.

No research-data deposit relevant to S1 or S2 was confirmed. The empty deposits list is intentional: the article and the commercial stimulus-generator website are not counted as deposits. The stimulus URL https://ideasai.net/ returned HTTP 200 after redirecting to https://ideasai.com/. The current page is titled 'Startup Ideas powered by xAI Grok', displays AI-generated ideas, and has no paper-name match or linked research-data repository/download file. It does not establish availability of the original GPT-3 stimulus pool or the randomized-study participants' records.

The article DOI returned HTTP 200 at an Elsevier Linking Hub redirect page. The ScienceDirect article landing page returned HTTP 403, so separate publisher supplementary files could not be inspected. The journal-homepage link also ended at HTTP 403. No credentials were used, no account or access request was made, and no access barrier was bypassed.

Searches covered the exact title, title keywords, and the first author's name, including the inverted form. OSF's Sorin title filter returned 17 public nodes; all titles/descriptions were inspected and unrelated (mostly substring matches to censoring or sensorineural, plus Carmen Sorin's Quick Files). The separate OSF full-name user search for Nathan Sorin returned zero profiles. No matching deposit identifier was found, so repository file-listing endpoints and participant-data downloads were not applicable.

Zenodo initially returned HTTP 400 because unauthenticated page size cannot exceed 25; both queries succeeded with size=25 and returned zero results. The additional broad DataCite search Sorin AND Nathan could not be fully evaluated: the first request returned HTTP 502, a size=25 response exceeded the in-memory read limit and could not be parsed (its HTTP status was not retained), and a sparse-field retry timed out. Their counts and relevance are null. Exact-name, inverted-name, exact-title, and title-keyword DataCite searches succeeded with zero matches. OSF search counts refer to nodes except the users API entry, which counts user profiles.

No additional statistics from final.open_items can be computed from verified public participant data. In particular, participant-level similarity uncertainty, unrounded similarity contrasts, the Study 2 idea-selection and exclusion rules, the Study 1 stimulus-pool analysis, usefulness-item composition, and idea-length results remain unresolved. Published aggregate means, SDs and counts are already in the screening form; they are not a participant-data release. The request-based policy is explicit, but confidence in the absence of a separate public deposit is medium because publisher supplementation and the broad DataCite query could not be completely checked.
